newsitem.title: UK: Halifax responds to UK base rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Halifax responds to UK base rate rise.

text.p: Britain's biggest building society, the Halifax, said it has launched a new range of mortgage products making it slightly more expensive for new borrowers to take out a mortgage.

"Overall, it makes it slightly more expensive to take out a new mortgage with us," said Gary Marsh, head of group corporate affairs. The Halifax is leaving its variable rate unchanged at 6.99 percent. The new range of products which take effect from November 21, include the removal of repayment fees on all discounted variable rates.
But fixed and discounted rates for two to five years will start at 5.29 percent for a two year loan for existing customers moving home, compared with 4.99 percent.
However cashbacks of as much as 10,000 stg are still available.

In a statement Mike Blackburn, Halifax chief executive said "With the continued recovery in the housing market and the recent bank base rate rise we are positioning our mortgage rates at a sensible level to avoid over-stimulation in the market."
The Halifax's decision follows the Nationwide's move on Tuesday to increase its standard variable rate by 0.25 percentage points to 6.74 percent.
